345749.title: The ironic decoration conjecture
345749.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $d_v$ be the degree of $v$, and assign a number $f(v)$ to each vertex. Define $M(v)=f(v)d_v$. An assignment is **ironic** if $M(u)\ne M(v)$ for every adjacent pair $u,v$. **The ironic decoration conjecture.** Every graph $G$ has an ironic decoration by the set $\{1,2,\dots,\chi(G)\}$. The claim is trivially true for regular graphs, but remains open in general.

347082.title: The circular chromatic conjecture for planar graphs
347082.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least $2t$. The **circular chromatic conjecture.**

$$
\chi_c(G)\le 2+\frac{2}{t}.
$$

The cases $t=1$ and $t=2$ follow from the Four Color Theorem and Grötzsch's theorem, respectively, while the conjecture remains open for every $t\ge 3$. It is known for $K_4$-minor-free graphs, a subclass of planar graphs.

353680.title: The conjecture on infinitely many grids with discrepancy 2
353680.statement: Let $d_n$ denote the discrepancy associated with the grid of size $n$. **The discrepancy-2 conjecture.** There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n=2$. 367473.title: Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's girth conjecture for Wenger-type graphs
367473.statement:
Let $D(k,q)$ be the graph defined by the parameters $k$ and the prime power $q$. **Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's conjecture.** For every prime power $q\ge 4$, the graph has girth

$$
\operatorname{girth}(D(k,q))=
\begin{cases}
k+5, & k\text{ odd},\\
k+4, & k\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source records matching lower bounds and presents equality as conjectural; no general resolution is supplied.

review_depth.primary_body: focused passage/context read as described in notes; no whole-manuscript audit
